finding.claim: On a 401 the SDK runs a silent refresh against an authorization server chosen from the server-supplied WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL. The stored refresh_token and client_secret are then sent to that attacker-chosen token_endpoint. Nothing pins the AS used at login.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter in a 401 from the MCP server (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416)
finding.sink: POST to attacker-controlled token_endpoint with refresh_token in the form and client_secret in Basic auth (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:663-666, 696, 707)

trace.note: attempt_refresh called with that URL before interactive flow
AS metadata fetched from attacker issuer

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_url! requires HTTPS only (flow.rb:380-385); ensure_issuer_matches! compares attacker-supplied issuer to attacker discovery URL (flow.rb:402-412); resource_covers? satisfied by attacker PRM echoing server URL (discovery.rb:306-324); no stored issuer or token_endpoint pin in provider, in_memory_storage, or storage_backed_provider; refresh runs without user consent, unlike the full authorization flow.

finding.claim: The client issues an HTTPS GET to any URL supplied in WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata, with no private, loopback, or link-local address block. Blind SSRF from the client host, low value.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter from the MCP server

trace.note: protected_resource_metadata_urls includes the attacker URL first
Faraday GET issued from client host

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_url! HTTPS-only check (flow.rb:380-385); no IP or host denylist; response is JSON-parsed and errors surface only to the local caller, so the attacker gets success or failure only.
